component.name: Nishro Link
component.summary: One mouse and keyboard across your computers

description.p: Push the pointer off the edge of one screen and it carries on onto the next computer, with the keyboard following it. Nishro Link works between Windows and Linux (Wayland and X11).

ul.li: Add a computer by its name and a four-word password - no addresses
Arrange the screens to match your desk, with every monitor drawn
Wrap-around, and shake the mouse to find the pointer
Encrypted with X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, a fresh key every connection
Runs from boot, so it also works on the login and lock screens

screenshot.caption: The Home page: who has control, and the arrangement
Arranging the screens, with a copy of a machine for wrap-around
Devices: this device's password, the group, and devices nearby

description.p: A keyboard or mouse connected after Nishro Link started - a wireless one waking up, a Bluetooth one, one plugged back in - is now picked up within two seconds.
Runs on older systems too: Python 3.8 and later, so Ubuntu 20.04 and Debian 11 are supported. Fixes a device renamed while switched off failing to reconnect on Python 3.8.
The first public release. The link's encryption is now built on standard primitives - X25519, HKDF-SHA256 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 - and the documentation covers installing, using and securing it.
A cleaner window: one navigation pane with Settings and Help at its foot, as in Windows' own Settings, and a Help page with About.
Windows and menus open cleanly - no flash - and menus open four times faster.
Shake the mouse to find the pointer, and less lag on Wi-Fi.
Resize any screen's box so borders meet exactly where you want, place copies of a machine for wrap-around, and a new icon.
Follows a dark desktop theme on Ubuntu, and the Windows setup no longer reports a failed service that in fact started.
A light and a dark theme that follow the system, Windows 11-style controls, a menu bar with Help and About, and the version shown.
Encryption, word passwords, adding and managing devices from any computer, a system service for the login and lock screens, and a new look.
